verified statement: The core complaint holds. The volume grades mₚ/mₑ = 6π⁵ as [F] "forced" in six places: the W.0 scorecard, the RF forced list and forced-coefficient ledger, the §13.5 "[F] identity" card, the header card, and registry/vp_locks.csv (grade F). Yet it carries a −18.82 ppm residual and no declared theory-error budget. As an exact identity it is excluded at about 1.08×10⁶σ against CODATA 2022 (3.1×10⁵σ against CODATA 2018).

This contradicts the volume's own taxonomy. The prologue defines [H] as covering "closures, idealizations, approximations, model choices", and forbids "retroactively promoting [H] to [F]". BT then says mₚ/mₑ was "upgraded from [H] to [F]".

§1.10(i) says a residual is "not a legitimate falsifier". Combined with that, the headline ratio cannot be refuted by any measurement. That also clashes with §1.4, which requires tolerances to be pre-registered.

The §1.8.3 "self-falsification" script cannot fail in practice. Every assert but one is an arithmetic or lattice-count fact. The one physical assert tests |μ/π⁵ − 6| = 1.129e-4 against a tolerance of 2e-4 (33 ppm). That tolerance is 1.77× the known residual and is tied to no declared budget. So the sentence "if a reader's run prints anything other than ALL PASS, the framework is wrong" misdescribes the test. The appendix r_p assert (5e-4, i.e. 500 ppm) is likewise loose next to the +61 ppm it checks.

**Overstated parts:**
- **The 5π closure is already graded [H].** §13.3.7 says "Grade: [F] for the geometric factor 5π …; [H] for closing the coefficient at the −0.40% level", and W.0 grades the m_H row "[F]/[H]". So the 4.6σ Higgs pull (−3.3σ vs PDG-2022) is attached to an [H] closure, not an [F] exact claim. What remains is an inconsistency: RF lists "the Higgs coefficient 5π" as Forced and §1.8.1 lists "canonical reduction integer 5π" under "Geometry (no DOF)", while BT puts 5π at step 2 (i.e. still [H]). There is also still no theory-error budget, and nothing says whether −4.6σ is acceptable.
- **Lenz is cited, and "fitted" is too strong.** The prologue does cite Lenz 1951 ("Lenz 1951 for mₚ/mₑ=6π⁵ as numerical coincidence"); it is §8.0.5 and §13.5 that omit it. LOCK-NU-N has no continuous parameter, so "fitted afterwards" overstates it. The accurate charge is accommodation: VH v0.2.1 shows the discrete law was adopted after 6π⁵ was known, when r_p had been a free input. The EA v40 log's relabel ("so that external readers do not read the Lenz mention as a concession…") also conflicts with the prologue's surviving "numerical coincidence" wording.
- **The σ-pull is a framing, not the core point.** The authors implicitly treat 6π⁵ as approximate: they report the residual, and §1.9 A3 admits "each individual residual could be a coincidence". So the ~10⁶σ number matters only because the grade is [F] with no correction budget. The defect is grading and falsifiability, not the arithmetic coincidence, which is genuinely unlikely: P ≈ 4×10⁻⁴ for n·π^k.

Severity stays critical. The headline number of the root volume is mis-graded against the volume's own definitions, and the falsification rule exempts it from data.

verified statement: The circularity is real, and it goes further than the reports say. I checked it independently.

(1) The locked 80-digit A in §11.3 [D-11.3-3] is exactly c·(1.86×10⁻²¹ s)/a. It carries only the 3 significant figures of a round Δt. §11.3.3 then presents Δt = A·a/c_ref as "the derived result". That is a round trip, so "cΔt/a=A closes exactly" is a tautology. The repro SSOT tool treats DT = 1.86e-21 as the input and calls A_geo a "⚠placeholder".

(2) A_geo := cΔt/a is the same number as A_lock. Its "0.16%" agreement with the SOC simulation cannot be reproduced from the published numbers:
- rescaled with N_ref = 200 it gives +0.35% against the mean and −16.05% against the median;
- 0.16% would need N_ref ≈ 201;
- the cited verify_A_scaling.py is not in the repository.

(3) D-11.3-3 defines A as the propagation length per tick divided by a, i.e. the lattice speed in cells per tick, and §11.3.3 defines c_ref := A·a/Δt. So c_env(SI) = c̃_env·(a/Δt) = c_ref·c̃_env/A, and c_env = c_ref is a unit identity, not the "shows it" result that A1 claims with grade [F]. A1 also uses c_ref as the agreement target, which is the move the chapter's own FAIL-CREF-PREDICT label forbids.

(4) Tₑ = (D/a)³·Δt·6/5 = 1.0058 s is linear in the placeholder Δt: with Δt = 1.85e-21 s it gives 1.0004 s. It also mixes two different A values. D = 4.853 pm implies A_D = 2πλ/D = 819,535, which is 7.0% below A_lock = 880,919. If one A is used for both D and Δt, Tₑ ∝ 1/A², which gives 0.81 s (A_lock), 0.936 s (A_D) or 0.977 s (A_med N=200). So Tₑ and A_geo are neither independent of each other nor valid entries in the A3 five-coincidence count.

(5) W.5.1 and the W.6 row say "Δt from a/c_ref". But a/c_ref = 2.11×10⁻²⁷ s, and the factor A is missing.

(6) New point: λ_ref = 632.99121257859865746 nm equals c/f_HeNe, with f = 473 612 353 604 kHz (CIPM), to all 20 digits. So Δt = A/(N·f): c cancels, and Δt is A/N times an external clock period referenced to the Cs second.

Mitigation, to be fair to the author: the volume partly acknowledges the problem. SP objection (iii) says "Acknowledged as a residual … whether Δt is independent of c (open, S5)". §11.6.5 says "anchored (to c,Δt,a; cf. the input-dependence honestly noted in §W.5)". §3.4 calls long numerals "computational placeholder[s]". The W.6 honest-reading note says A's magnitude tracks 1/g₀. These acknowledgements are not applied elsewhere, though. §11.3, the A1 grade [F], the A3 count, W.0 ("measured from the lattice … not a free fit") and SP ("anchored … to 0.16%") still present these items as derivations or evidence.

What survives legitimately: a single longitudinal signal speed with c² = B/ρ in lattice units (§11.6.1, graded [V]). The SI value of c, Δt, the 0.16%, and the Tₑ ≈ 1 s residual do not survive as evidence.

verified statement: The claim that the framework has a "single empirical anchor (DOF = 1)" is false by the volume's own tables and code, so the "formal proof" in §1.8 does not hold.

What the outputs actually depend on:
- **Two independent measured continuous anchors:**
  - λ_ref = 632.99 nm, through a = λ_ref/N, which feeds U_lat and m_H.
  - The CODATA electron mass, through D_anch = 2λ_C,e, which feeds r_p, m_p, χ, τ_q and T_e.
- **N = 10¹²:** a declared split integer that is never derived. m_H is proportional to N.

Why it fails as registered: with sinχ = x/⌈x⌉ and x = λ/D, χ is a sawtooth in frac(x). It is bounded to (89.776°, 90°] at 633 nm and (89.755°, 90°] at 532 nm for any D. So:
(a) "0.03% in D ⇒ >1° in χ" is impossible. The maximum swing is 0.224°.
(b) D's declared 0.04% precision spans about 52 sawtooth periods (one period = 7.67 ppm in D), and the declared "stated width" (the ℓ_rot / D-distribution spread) spans thousands. The committed window is therefore the whole band.
(c) The committed numbers are artifacts of rounded inputs. The volume's own full-precision λ_ref gives 89.7960°, and the real I₂-stabilised 532.245 nm line gives 89.9680°.
(d) A χ measurement fixes D only modulo 7.67 ppm (aliasing), so it cannot "pin D to 0.001%" or choose among candidate D values.
(e) The "falsifiable" ratio 1.189831 is just 632.99/532.0, an identity.
(f) "χ=90° never reached" is false whenever λ/D is an integer, and the visible row "89.8°–89.9°" is really 89.71°–90°.

Where the reports overstate: the window does not rule out *nothing*. The spine (SP S2.3, graded [V]) and §11.6.1 say that at isostaticity G_relaxed→0 while B stays finite, so "the transverse wave dies; one longitudinal speed survives, c²=B/ρ". The hub title and the w0 scorecard then identify c with the speed of light, and w0 grades that identification [V].

Chapter 14 relies on the opposite:

- It states that photons carry helicity ±1.

In an isotropic elastic continuum the transverse (divergence-free) sector travels at c_T²=G/ρ, and the spine itself drives that to 0. It does not travel at √(B/ρ). The one mode that survives, u=∇φ, is scalar: one polarization, helicity 0. So the [V] result removes the sector that §14.0.6 needs and keeps the one that light lacks.

It is critical for Chapter 18's headline claim, which the hub states as "the river identity makes gravitational time dilation exact Schwarzschild. forced". Three secondary sub-claims in the reports are overstated or aimed at the wrong target; they are listed at the end.

(1) G-RIVER is an algebraic identity. It sets v_river := sqrt(2GM/r), then checks sqrt(1 - v_river^2/c^2) == sqrt(1 - 2GM/rc^2) with floating-point equality. That holds for any G, M and r, so "machine-exact from the Moon to a neutron star" has no power to tell theories apart. The chapter (§18.6 "verifies ... to machine precision", §18.8 "G-RIVER passes"), the scorecard (W.0, [F]) and the hub still present it as a forced or verified result. None of these texts, and nothing in docs/physics or repro/physics, cites Painlevé–Gullstrand or Hamilton & Lisle, even though this is exactly their "river" form of GR. §18.0 also claims "No external relativistic postulate is used".

(2) The escape speed is not the velocity the medium actually has in the framework's own mechanics. The volume's own void-forbidden continuity is "4πφ r²v=QₛV_q ⇒ 1/r²" (§17.4.4(ii)). §18.0 says a clock slows by "its velocity relative to the local medium". Feeding this flow into that rule gives dilation growing as r^-4, not r^-1. Gravity Probe A and the Galileo-5/6 eccentric-orbit redshift tests measured the r^-1 dependence to about 1e-4 and about 3e-5 respectively. The magnitude is also wrong: ×301 at the surface under M1, and ×120 to ×1100 across the M1–M4 conventions.

§18.7's "two velocities" device says the clock uses a "potential velocity" sqrt(-2φ_N) instead. But it never derives why a clock would couple to that velocity rather than to the medium's actual motion. That contradicts §18.0 and §18.9's v_loc = "relative to the inflow".

(3) The alternative also fails. A steady flow with v ∝ r^-1/2 would need either ρ ∝ r^-3/2, so that c = sqrt(K/ρ) varies with radius (c(2R)/c(R) = 1.68), or absorption spread through all of space. Both contradict the point-sink, incompressible, constant-c picture.

(4) §18.8 says orbits, light bending and gravitational waves "equal exact Schwarzschild by §18.6". But §18.6 only gives the static clock rate (g_tt). No calculation of light bending, Shapiro delay or perihelion shift (PPN γ and β) exists anywhere in the volume. My grep found only that sentence.

That signature matches what Super-K's p→e⁺γ searches look for (two back-to-back showers of about 469 MeV). Nucleon-decay limits of about 10³³–10³⁴ yr (for example τ(p→e⁺π⁰) > 2.4×10³⁴ yr) are about 1.7×10²⁴ times the age of the universe, so the departure as written conflicts with some of the most tightly constrained facts in physics.

(a) p→e⁺π⁰ follows only generically: it would need pion states that the volume never builds. The direct and unavoidable consequence is H→γγ.
(b) The single-photon form "γ→p⁺e⁻" is forbidden by kinematics in vacuum anyway. Elsewhere in the same chapter the volume correctly writes γγ→e⁺e⁻, so it should say γγ→p e⁻ or γZ→p e⁻ Z.
(c) The claimed payoff also fails on its own terms. The text also defers this payoff to "the separate cosmology whitepaper", but the cosmology volume contains no matching content (a grep of docs/cosmology for baryon number / antimatter / p+e returns nothing).

### [59] The integerization formula breaks sum preservation for N≡2 (mod 3) and cannot produce the splits used  (severity: major; category: math-error; verdict: confirmed)
locations: 07 'Definition of real-valued sector scores s_i' (symmetric-input output eq.), 'Integerization (sum-preserving) rule', §7.1.3–§7.1.5
verified statement: Every factual claim checks out, and one framing point needs softening. (a) The perfectly-symmetric (S=0) branch of the locked integerization rule (ch. 07, eq. phy-07-009, extraction line 94) gives (⌊N/3⌋,⌊N/3⌋,⌈N/3⌉) for every N≢0 (mod 3). For N≡2 (mod 3) that sums to N−1, which breaks the chapter's own invariant k₁+k₂+k₃=N (e.g. 89→(29,29,30), sum 88). The same chapter states the correct form, (m,m+1,m+1), in §7.1.3.2 and §7.2.3, so this is an internal inconsistency. (b) The S>0 projection/largest-remainder branch shifts s_i=p_i−p_min, so at least one f_i is 0. That sector has residual 0 and can never receive a +1. The deficit is then Δ∈{0,1}, not {0,1,2} as stated. So every S>0 output has min k_i=0. The fractions f_i depend only on the direction of u, not its size, so an arbitrarily small u≠0 already gives an empty sector: the rule jumps from (m,m,m+r) at u=0 to a maximally biased split, e.g. (89,0,0). (c) The splits 89→(30,30,29) and 82→(28,27,27) come only from the §7.1 minimum-variance rule with π_sec, which takes no u. Steelman: §7.1 can be read as the fuller statement of the S=0 branch, with the nucleon totals treated as sector-symmetric inputs. Read that way, the two rules are complementary branches rather than 'incompatible', but the chapter never says so. The downstream numbers (30,30,29) and (28,27,27) are themselves correct. The defect is in the stated/locked rule and in where the chapter says those numbers come from, not in the numbers.
